verses.1: For the music director. A psalm of David.
verses.2: The heavens declare the glory of God; the vault proclaims the work of his hands.
verses.3: One day tells another, and one night tells the next what is known.
verses.4: There are no words, there are no utterances, yet their voice is not unheard.
verses.5: Their message has gone out into all the earth, and their words to the ends of the world. The sun has placed its tent among them.
verses.6: And it is like a bridegroom coming from his wedding canopy, rejoicing like a warrior running his course.
verses.7: From the end of the heavens is its rising, and its reaching is to the ends of the heavens. There is no one who hides from its heat.
verses.8: The teaching of the LORD is perfect, restoring the soul. The testimony of the LORD is trustworthy, making the simple wise.
verses.9: The commandments of the LORD are right, giving joy to the heart. The instruction of the LORD is clear, lighting the eyes.
verses.10: The fear of the LORD is pure, enduring forever. The judgments of the LORD are true, altogether righteous.
verses.11: They are more desirable than gold, more than much fine gold; and sweeter than honey, yes, than the drippings of the honeycomb.
verses.12: Indeed, by keeping them your servant is warned, and in keeping them there is a great reward.
verses.13: Who can know their faults? Cleanse me from my hidden faults,
verses.14: and keep your servant from willful sin, that they may not rule over me. Then I will be blameless, and cleansed from great iniquity.
verses.15: May the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable in your sight, LORD, my rock and my redeemer.

notes:
Notes
- v. 11: "than the drippings of the honeycomb" — the Hebrew uses נֹפֶת צוּפִֽים (nō·p̄eṯ ṣō·p̄îm), often translated as "honeycomb," but the comparative "than" is retained for poetic emphasis.
- v. 15: "acceptable in your sight" — the Hebrew uses לְרָצֹון (lə·rā·ṣō·w·n), meaning "for acceptance" or "for favor."
